title: Chapter 40 — Follow-Up Closing & The Second-Visit Close
intro: Closing the sale that left the floor — the phone close, the return visit, and the re-quote moment.

sections.title: The Follow-Up Cadence
sections.content:
Most appliance quotes die of silence, not rejection. Here is the system.

Day 0 — same day: send a thank-you text within 2 hours of their visit. Include your name, the store, and the quote summary.

Day 1: email the formal quote PDF. Include product images, specs, and pricing. Mention the promotion deadline if one exists.

Day 3: call. Not text, not email — a phone call. 'Hi [name], this is [you] from [store]. I wanted to check in and see if any questions came up about the [product] we looked at.'

Day 7: send a value-add. A comparison chart, a review article, an installation video. Show you are thinking about their purchase, not just chasing a commission.

Day 14: the honest check-in. 'I know life gets busy. I wanted to let you know that the product is still available and your quote is still valid. No pressure.'

Day 30: the long-game touch. If they are still thinking, they are still interested. Keep the door open.

sections.title: Rules for Every Follow-Up
sections.content:
Never guilt. Never pressure. Never say 'just following up' — that phrase communicates zero value. Every touch should give them something: information, reassurance, or convenience. Stop if they ask you to stop.

Track everything. Log every touch in the CRM. Tag the reason for no-close. The patterns tell you where your floor process is breaking.

sections.title: The Second-Visit Close
sections.content:
When a customer returns, they are almost always ready to buy. Do not start from scratch. Pull up their quote. Reference what they told you last time. Show them you remember.

'Welcome back. I have your quote right here — the Bosch 500 series we looked at last week. Has anything changed or are we good to go?'

The returning customer has already done their thinking. They just need confirmation and a gentle push to the finish line.
